name: British Broadcasting Corporation
tagline: Nation Shall Speak Peace Unto Nation — Public Service Broadcasting & Digital Media
headquarters: Broadcasting House, Portland Place, London W1A 1AA
governance: BBC Board, led by Chair and Director-General Tim Davie, regulated by Ofcom

overview: The BBC is the world’s leading public service broadcaster, providing impartial news, television, radio, BBC iPlayer, BBC Sounds, and educational content to millions of daily users across the UK and internationally. Its web and mobile platforms handle hundreds of millions of daily requests with strict uptime, accessibility, and editorial accuracy mandates.
heroHeadline: Inform, Educate and Entertain in the Digital Era
heroSubtext: Discover how the BBC delivers 24/7 global news, high-definition streaming on BBC iPlayer, radio on BBC Sounds, and educational resources powered by cloud-native web architecture and resilient infrastructure.

services.title: BBC News Multi-Platform
services.description: Continuous 24-hour breaking news, regional UK reports, live text commentaries, and impartial verified reporting.
services.technicalDelivery: Distributed microservices architecture delivering dynamic JSON feeds cached across Tier-1 CDN edge servers in sub-50ms latency.
services.audience: UK public and global readership (over 450m weekly users).

services.title: BBC iPlayer Video-on-Demand
services.description: Ultra HD 4K, HDR, and live TV streaming of BBC One, Two, Three, Four, and extensive boxsets with parental controls and TV Licence verification.
services.technicalDelivery: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR) using HLS and MPEG-DASH formats with DRM encryption and edge-cached video segments.
services.audience: UK licence-fee payers accessing via web browsers, smart TVs, mobile apps, and consoles.

services.title: BBC Sounds Audio Platform
services.description: Live broadcast of 10 national radio stations, 40+ local stations, on-demand podcasts, curated music mixes, and offline downloads.
services.technicalDelivery: Real-time AAC/MP3 audio stream ingestion through AWS Elemental MediaStore with GraphQL metadata aggregation.
services.audience: Audio listeners seeking news, drama, comedy, and music curation.

services.title: BBC Bitesize Educational Portal
services.description: Curriculum-aligned revision materials, interactive quizzes, video tutorials, and study aids for KS1, KS2, KS3, GCSE, and National 5 students.
services.technicalDelivery: Accessible static-generated HTML5 modules with interactive React assessment engines and high WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility scoring.
services.audience: UK primary, secondary students, teachers, and home-educating parents.

services.title: BBC Sport Real-Time Centre
services.description: Live scores, football tables, Premier League match commentaries, Formula 1 telemetry, and video highlights packages.
services.technicalDelivery: Low-latency WebSocket connections and Server-Sent Events (SSE) pushing instant score changes directly to client viewports.
services.audience: Sports fans wanting instant, verified match updates.

services.title: BBC Weather Forecast Service
services.description: Pinpoint hourly UK and international weather forecasts, rain radars, UV warnings, and severe weather alert banners.
services.technicalDelivery: Ingestion of Met Office gridded meteorological API data parsed into spatial GeoJSON layers and rendered via client-side vector charts.
services.audience: General public and UK emergency planning authorities.

architecture.summary: The BBC operates one of the world’s most sophisticated cloud-native web architectures. Built upon its internal Global Experience Language (GEL) and micro-frontends framework, the platform decouples editorial content authoring from multi-channel delivery using headless CMS engines, AWS multi-region infrastructure, and geo-distributed CDN caching.
architecture.diagramDescription: Editorial staff publish through the CPS/Nitro CMS -> Stored in DynamoDB & Aurora -> GraphQL Federation layer aggregates entities -> Edge CDN nodes (Fastly & Akamai) cache HTML/JSON -> Client browser receives semantic HTML5 + modern CSS/JS bundles with progressive enhancement.

components.title: HTML5 Semantic Markup & Accessibility
components.explanation: HTML forms the foundational skeleton of every BBC webpage. The BBC uses strict semantic tags such as <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, and <footer>. This semantic clarity ensures that assistive technologies (screen readers like JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver) can interpret page hierarchies effortlessly. Headings (H1 to H6) follow strict sequential numbering without skipping levels.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Semantic HTML improves search engine ranking (SEO) by defining meaningful content boundaries, enables web crawlers to categorize news topics, and complies with UK Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations (PSBAR 2018).
components.implementationExample:
UK Inflation Drops to Target

15 September 2026

Consumer prices index figures released this morning show...

components.title: Cascading Style Sheets (CSS3 & GEL)
components.tech: CSS3, Modern CSS Grid, Flexbox, BBC Global Experience Language (GEL)
components.explanation: CSS controls typography, visual hierarchy, colour contrast, and responsive layout across phones, tablets, smart TVs, and desktop monitors. The BBC GEL framework enforces mathematical font sizing (BBC Reith font family), consistent 8px spatial grid gutters, and strict 4.5:1 minimum colour contrast ratios to guarantee readability.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Fluid CSS Grid and media queries (@media (min-width: 768px)) ensure responsive reflow without horizontal scrolling, reducing mobile bounce rates and data consumption.

components.title: JavaScript & Progressive Enhancement
components.tech: TypeScript, ES2022, React, Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Web Workers
components.explanation: JavaScript powers interactive components such as the iPlayer video scrubber, live score tickers, navigation drawers, and weather search autocomplete. Crucially, the BBC follows the "Progressive Enhancement" philosophy: core news text is pre-rendered on the server so if a user has JavaScript disabled or suffers a slow connection, the article remains fully readable.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Code-splitting and tree-shaking prevent oversized JS bundles, keeping initial Time-to-Interactive (TTI) under 2.0 seconds over 4G mobile networks.

components.title: Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)
components.tech: RESTful JSON APIs, GraphQL Apollo Federation, WebSocket Streams
components.explanation: APIs connect the user-facing web applications to back-end editorial databases and media streaming encoders. The BBC uses GraphQL federation to allow front-end components to query only the precise fields needed (e.g. headline, thumbnail, publishedTimestamp), eliminating over-fetching.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Rate limiting and API gateway throttling prevent denial-of-service spikes during major breaking news broadcasts (e.g., General Elections).

components.title: Content Management System (CMS)
components.tech: BBC CPS (Content Production System), Headless Nitro Editorial Engine
components.explanation: Journalists in London, Salford, Glasgow, and worldwide author articles, audio clips, and video bulletins within CPS. The CMS validates editorial standards, spelling, copyright licensing, and legal defamation checks before pushing articles to the publishing pipeline.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Decoupled (headless) CMS architecture separates the authoring UI from presentation servers, preventing editorial bottlenecks from affecting public-facing web uptime.
components.implementationExample: CMS Workflow: Author Draft -> Senior Editor Review -> Legal Compliance Flag -> Digital Asset Metadata Tagging -> Automated Publish to S3 & CDN Flush.

components.title: Database Layer & Data Storage
components.tech: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, AWS DynamoDB, Redis Cluster, Amazon S3
components.explanation: The BBC uses a polyglot persistence strategy. Structured relational data (user accounts, permissions, TV licence validation) resides in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with multi-Availability Zone replication. High-velocity unstructured data (live article comments, telemetry, programme metadata) is stored in Amazon DynamoDB for millisecond key-value retrieval, backed by Redis in-memory caching.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: ACID compliance in PostgreSQL guarantees that account data cannot become corrupted during simultaneous transactions.
components.implementationExample: SELECT user_id, licence_status, expiry_date FROM bbc_accounts WHERE email_hash = $1;

components.title: Cloud Hosting & Infrastructure
components.tech: Amazon Web Services (AWS eu-west-1 & eu-west-2), Kubernetes (EKS)
components.explanation: Rather than maintaining physical on-premise servers for web delivery, the BBC hosts its digital estate in AWS multi-region infrastructure. Containerised microservices run inside Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) pods that automatically scale up or down based on incoming CPU load and network traffic.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Auto-scaling allows the BBC to surge from 10,000 requests per second to 250,000 requests per second within three minutes during major national events.
components.implementationExample: Kubernetes HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler): MinReplicas: 20, MaxReplicas: 400, TargetCPUUtilization: 65%.

components.title: Content Delivery Network (CDN) & Edge Caching
components.tech: Fastly & Akamai Multi-CDN Architecture, Anycast DNS, Varnish (VCL)
components.explanation: The BBC utilizes a multi-CDN strategy combining Fastly and Akamai. When a user requests an article or an iPlayer video segment, the request is routed to the geographically nearest CDN Point of Presence (PoP) in London, Manchester, Edinburgh, or Belfast. 95%+ of all requests are served directly from cache memory.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: CDNs absorb distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) volumetric attacks before malicious requests can touch the BBC origin servers.
components.implementationExample:
HTTP/2 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300
X-Cache: HIT from Fastly-LHR

components.title: HTTPS, SSL/TLS 1.3 & Transport Security
components.tech: TLS 1.3, Strict Transport Security (HSTS), Perfect Forward Secrecy
components.explanation: Every connection to bbc.co.uk is enforced over HTTPS using TLS 1.3 encryption. HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) with preloading in modern browsers instructs the browser to never communicate over unencrypted HTTP, preventing Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) eavesdropping.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Encryption protects users reading sensitive political, health, or investigative journalism from being monitored by third parties on open Wi-Fi networks.
components.implementationExample:
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' https://*.bbc.co.uk;

components.title: User Authentication & BBC ID
components.tech: BBC Account Identity Service, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), JWT
components.explanation: BBC ID allows users to sign in, verify their TV Licence declaration, save programmes to their iPlayer watchlist, and resume podcast playback across devices. Passwords are salted and hashed using Argon2/bcrypt algorithms. JSON Web Tokens (JWT) manage short-lived stateless sessions.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Token-based stateless authentication allows millions of users to remain authenticated across auto-scaled microservices without central session database locks.

components.title: System Monitoring, Telemetry & Observability
components.tech: Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, Synthetic User Monitors
components.explanation: BBC engineering teams monitor thousands of metrics per second: HTTP 5xx error rates, page load latency (LCP/FID/CLS), video buffer ratios, and database connection pools. Automated synthetic probes test login and playback every 60 seconds from external UK internet providers.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Real-time alerting via PagerDuty notifies on-call DevOps engineers when error rates exceed 0.05% of total traffic.
components.implementationExample: Alert Rule: IF rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[2m]) / rate(http_requests_total[2m]) > 0.005 THEN alert_oncall_engineer();

components.title: Disaster Recovery & Automated Backup Strategy
components.tech: Multi-Region Active-Active Replication, Automated Daily Snapshots, RTO/RPO
components.explanation: To satisfy public service broadcasting resilience mandates, BBC data is replicated continuously between AWS London (eu-west-2) and AWS Ireland (eu-west-1). If an entire cloud data centre experiences catastrophic failure, automated DNS failover redirects traffic within 30 seconds. Database snapshots are stored in immutable write-once-read-many (WORM) S3 buckets.
components.educationalLevel3Notes: Level 3 Assessment Note: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is under 5 minutes for core news services, and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is zero data loss for news copy.
components.implementationExample: RTO: < 5 mins | RPO: < 10 seconds | Cross-Region Automated Sync with Point-in-Time Database Recovery (PITR).

security.summary: As a high-profile national broadcaster and critical UK digital infrastructure provider, the BBC is continuously targeted by nation-state cyber adversaries, hacktivists, and phishing fraudsters. The BBC operates a dedicated Cyber Security Operations Centre (SOC) enforcing Defence-in-Depth, UK GDPR compliance, and ISO/IEC 27001 standards.
complianceStandards: UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR)

risks.threatName: Brand Impersonation & TV Licence Phishing Scams
risks.impactDescription: Criminal syndicates send fraudulent emails and SMS messages claiming the recipient’s "BBC TV Licence has expired" or "Payment failed", directing victims to counterfeit lookalike sites that steal banking details.
risks.attackVector: Email spoofing, SMS smishing, typo-squatted domain names (e.g. bbc-licence-renew.co.uk).
risks.mitigationStrategy: Deployment of DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication) with strict p=reject policy, active brand monitoring and legal takedown teams, customer education campaigns, and domain blocklisting via the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) Protective DNS.

risks.threatName: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) on Election Nights
risks.impactDescription: Malicious botnets attempt to flood BBC web servers with gigabits of garbage traffic during general elections or major royal broadcasts, aiming to censor news reporting and sow public panic.
risks.attackVector: SYN floods, UDP amplification, Layer 7 HTTP GET floods attacking un-cached search and live results endpoints.
risks.mitigationStrategy: Multi-layered DDoS protection via Fastly and Akamai Edge Scrubbing centres, rate limiting per IP, automatic CAPTCHA challenges for anomalous volumetric bursts, and direct peering with major UK ISPs.
risks.ukLegalFramework: Computer Misuse Act 1990 Section 3 (Unauthorised act with intent to impair computer operation).

risks.impactDescription: Attackers attempt to inject malicious JavaScript into live news comment sections, feedback forms, or search query parameters, which could steal session tokens or deface reputable headlines.
risks.attackVector: Reflected or stored XSS vulnerabilities in user-submitted comments or search input forms.
risks.mitigationStrategy: Strict Content Security Policy (CSP) blocking unauthorized script execution, automated HTML entity sanitisation (DOMPurify), React JSX automatic escaping, and disabling eval() functions.
risks.ukLegalFramework: Data Protection Act 2018, OWASP Top 10 A03: Injection.

risks.threatName: Account Takeover & Credential Stuffing on BBC ID
risks.impactDescription: Automated bots test millions of stolen username/password pairs obtained from third-party data breaches against the BBC ID login endpoint to hijack viewer accounts and scrape viewing habits.
risks.attackVector: Distributed credential stuffing attacks utilizing rotating residential proxy networks.
risks.mitigationStrategy: Web Application Firewall (WAF) bot detection, biometric and behavioural analysis, rate limiting, mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA) for staff accounts, and integration with "Have I Been Pwned" APIs to block compromised passwords.
risks.ukLegalFramework: UK GDPR Article 32 (Security of Processing), Data Protection Act 2018.

risks.impactDescription: Compromise of an open-source npm library or analytics SDK used on the BBC website could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code or spy on user sessions.
risks.attackVector: Malicious dependencies in node_modules, compromised CI/CD build pipelines, outdated third-party scripts.
risks.mitigationStrategy: Automated Dependabot and Snyk vulnerability scanning in GitHub Actions, Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) tracking, Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes on external assets, and strict vendor security audits.
risks.ukLegalFramework: ISO 27001 Annex A.15 (Supplier Relationships), NCSC Supply Chain Security Guidance.

security.incidentResponsePlan: The BBC CSIRT follows the NCSC 5-phase Incident Response Framework: 1) Identification & Triage (24/7 SOC automated alerting); 2) Containment (network isolation, edge CDN blocking); 3) Eradication (root-cause patch deployment, credential revocation); 4) Recovery (phased service restoration with active synthetic monitoring); 5) Post-Incident Lessons Learned and statutory reporting to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) within 72 hours where personal data is implicated.

reviews.author: David Henderson
reviews.title: Essential educational tool with flawless uptime
reviews.comment: BBC Bitesize and the News round-up are integral to our morning classes. The website loads rapidly on school tablets, video clips play without buffering, and the absence of third-party commercial adverts keeps students focused.

reviews.author: Priya Sharma
reviews.title: Seamless audio switching between phone and smart speaker
reviews.comment: BBC Sounds allows me to start listening to the Today programme on my kitchen smart speaker and continue on the train via my smartphone app without losing my timestamp. Exemplary digital design and accessibility.

reviews.author: Alistair Campbell
reviews.title: Clear typography and easy-to-read layout
reviews.comment: As someone with impaired eyesight, I appreciate the high contrast text, large font controls, and screen reader compatibility. The BBC News website is by far the cleanest news source on the internet.

reviews.author: Megan O’Reilly
reviews.title: 4K Ultra HD streaming on BBC iPlayer is outstanding
reviews.comment: Watched the wildlife documentary series in 4K HDR on my smart TV. The adaptive bitrate streaming never dropped quality once. Truly sets the benchmark for British public broadcasting technology.

userFlow.flowName: BBC iPlayer Programme Playback & TV Licence Verification Flow
userFlow.objective: Map the complete technical journey of an audience member searching for a documentary, authenticating their BBC Account, verifying licence eligibility, and establishing an encrypted adaptive bitrate video stream.

steps.title: User Lands on BBC iPlayer & Enters Search Query
steps.action: Navigates to bbc.co.uk/iplayer and searches for "Planet Earth III" in the search bar.
steps.technicalDetails: Browser sends client-side debounced GET request to /api/v1/search?q=planet+earth with auto-suggest JSON response.
steps.failurePath: Zero search results returns curated trending programmes and spelling correction hints.

steps.title: Frontend Requests Programme Metadata
steps.action: Transmits GraphQL query to the BBC Apollo Federation Gateway.
steps.technicalDetails: GraphQL fetches programme UUID, synopsis, age rating (12), 4K video asset URLs, and subtitle tracks from Nitro CMS repository.

steps.title: BBC ID Authentication & TV Licence Verification Check
steps.action: Checks for active session JWT token and verifies TV Licence declaration status.
steps.technicalDetails: If no valid token is found, user is redirected to /account/signin with returnUrl query parameter. Postgres database checks user record.
steps.failurePath: If unauthenticated, user is prompted to sign in or create an account; playback paused.

steps.title: DRM Token Issuance & Geo-IP Location Validation
steps.action: Validates UK IP address via MaxMind GeoIP database and issues Widevine/FairPlay DRM license key.
steps.technicalDetails: Confirms client IP originates from the United Kingdom to comply with rights licensing. Issues encrypted session token.
steps.failurePath: If non-UK IP detected, displays informative "BBC iPlayer only works in the UK due to rights agreements" modal.

steps.title: Adaptive Bitrate Manifest Ingestion & Video Playback
steps.action: Client HTML5 video player requests m3u8 (HLS) or mpd (DASH) manifest from Fastly CDN.
steps.technicalDetails: Player measures available bandwidth every 2 seconds, dynamically adjusting bitrate between 1080p, 4K, and 720p chunks to eliminate buffering.

steps.title: Telemetry & Viewing Position Save to Redis
steps.action: Background beacon periodically transmits playback timestamp back to BBC Account service.
steps.technicalDetails: Saves resume timestamp (e.g., 24m:15s) into Redis cache so user can continue seamlessly on smart TV.
